text:
Jake Neighbours plays like his comparisons on this page: Jamie Benn, around the net, through traffic, and he hits (70 hits in 22 games, a lot for a top-nine scorer). He has 5 goals and 13 points, and the goals match his chances exactly. He just had a goal and an assist against Anaheim, including one off the rush with Robert Thomas, then two assists against Pittsburgh.

The flattering part is around him. St. Louis has scored about eight goals more than its chances with him on the ice, one of the biggest gaps in the league, while the Blues get under half the expected goals in his minutes. Expect the on-ice goals to cool even if he keeps finding his spots.

Last season Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.4 wins, 34th among forwards, but also noted that results ran well ahead of the chances. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains what makes him work when it works: 1.5 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, the kind that go in far more often. Watch his five-on-five share. If it climbs back toward even, the points will hold.
